relevance_note: UK Behçet's disease WES cohort in which 'Five patients (cases 5, 10, 14, 29, 31) were classified as having Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20)', each with individual-level data in Table 1.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown (main text, Table 1, Table 2, supplementary PDF text). Scope: the 5 HA20 cases (5, 10, 14, 29, 31) plus relatives described in relation to them: mother of Case 10 (affected, 'similar features'), mother of Case 14 (autoimmune hypothyroidism), mother of Case 29 (affected and carries p.C657Vfs*14), maternal grandmother and brother of Case 29 (milder symptoms; not found to carry the variant, but testing is not stated explicitly, so no variant rows). Case 29's 'maternal cousins' were not given rows because their number is not stated. The other 26 cohort members (other genes or no monogenic variant) get no rows; cohort size 31. Labels: Table 1 has a 'Case' column of bare numbers, but the text uses 'case N'/'Case N' for these people, so rule 1 gives 'Case N'. Table 1 spans quote the row from label through the cell where short; for cells right of the long Clinical features column (gene, variant, zygosity, classification, identification method) the span is the contiguous row segment from the Gene cell, which is unique per variant row; outcome/treatment spans quote the outcome cell. Age column = 'Age at the time of this study' (legend b), recorded as age at last evaluation. Variants: Table 1 prints nucleotide changes without 'c.' (e.g. '227C>T') and protein changes mostly without 'p.'; recorded as printed. No transcript printed (legend says HGNC RefSeq transcript, none named). Variant class not stated for any TNFAIP3 variant, so variant_type is 'not reported' (not derived from HGVS). Zygosity from the Zygosity column 'Het' (legend 'Het: heterozygous'). Pathogenicity from the 'Variant classification' column (value 3), whose coding is given in Methods ('Class 3: unknown significance'). Functional evidence: NF-kB assay group statement names cases 5, 14, 29 and 31; for Case 29 the supplementary legend gives his own different result (less activation, attributed to treatment), which is recorded instead of the group statement. Case 10 'was unavailable for follow-up testing', so functional evidence is 'not reported'. No table symbol or stacked cell was used to exclude anything; no excluded features were recorded. Case 5's transaminitis (colchicine adverse effect) was not recorded as a disease feature; it appears in treatment_summary. Contradictions/discrepancies: (1) Case 10 has two TNFAIP3 rows in Table 1 (946G>A G316S and 1625_1626insGAC TACAGCAGAGGCC S548Dfs*128), but the abstract/results list only p.S548Dfs*128 among the 'five novel heterozygous variants'; both rows recorded. (2) Case 14: Table 1 says 'chronic pulmonary interstitial emphysema', the Results text says 'chronic interstitial pneumonia'; both recorded as features; interstitial lung disease checklist marked observed from the text statement. (3) Table 1 gives all TNFAIP3 variants classification 3 (unknown significance), whereas the Discussion states that six of the seven novel proposed disease-causing variants 'can be classified as pathogenic according to the ACMG criteria' with only p.T76I remaining a VUS; recorded the per-row table value (plus the explicit VUS statement for Case 5). (4) Results say NF-kB assay 'showed upregulation of the pathway in all four cases' but the supplementary legend says Case 29 'showed less activation'. Checklist judgement calls: Case 5 'redness of the eyes' not mapped to ocular inflammation; headaches not mapped to CNS involvement; perianal ulcers (Cases 29, 31) not by themselves mapped to GI ulcers (Case 29's GI item is observed from colitis); Case 31 'recurrent tonsilitis' not mapped to recurrent infections; Case 29 livedo reticularis mapped to skin lesions; autoimmune hypothyroidism mapped to autoimmune thyroiditis. A Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON from values typed from my reading; every span was checked verbatim against the paper.
